title: adaptive-kernel-selection-and-fused-rotary-reshape-with-kv-reservation
author: Evan Grant
description:
Motivation: long-tail inference workloads (mixed sequence lengths and multi-tenant bursts) expose inefficiencies in a single-kernel dispatch strategy and occasionally trigger noisy KV cache pressure. This PR implements an adaptive kernel selector that chooses between two optimized attention kernels at runtime (small-seq fastpath + wide-seq streaming fastpath), introduces a small fused rotary-reshape CUDA kernel to remove redundant transposes when rotary embeddings are used, and adds a lightweight KV reservation mechanism to reduce eviction churn under bursty continuous-batching.

What this PR does (high level):
- Runtime kernel selector: heuristics based on sequence length, batch shape distribution, and available SM occupancy to pick best kernel per request group. Selector lives in serving/runtime/attn/kernel_selector.cpp and exposes a stable decision API so other schedulers can consult it.
- Fused rotary-reshape: new CUDA kernel fused_rotary_reshape.cu removes an intermediate permute and reduces memory traffic for rotary-enabled models (~1.6x reduction in transient mem ops on long sequences). Hooked into the kernel code path when rotary flags are detected.
- KV reservation: add kv_reservation.h/.cpp that lets the continuous batcher reserve a bounded KV budget for in-flight canary/cold requests so we avoid evicting hot prefixes during transient spikes. Implemented conservative default: 8% reservation per model instance, configurable in runtime config.
- Batching/backpressure tweaks: continuous_batcher now exposes a backpressure token check and will fall back to the small-seq kernel earlier to meet p95 latency SLOs for short requests.

Checklist: 
- [x] Kernel selector implementation + unit tests
- [x] CUDA fused rotary-reshape implementation + correctness tests
- [x] KV reservation mechanism + e2e smoke test
- [x] Bench harness changes and new benchmarks
- [x] Docs: perf rationale and flags in docs/perf/attn_kernels.md

Performance summary (bench running on p4d-like staging infra, mixed workload):
- End-to-end token throughput +13-17% on 2048-8192 seq mix for a 16-GPU pool when selector chooses wide-seq kernel.
- Memory transient traffic reduced ~1.6x for rotary models when fused kernel engaged.
- p95 latency for short seq requests unchanged (<2% regressions in noise runs).
- KV eviction events under bursty load reduced ~45% in microbench.

Compatibility and rollout: changes are backward-compatible. Selector defaults to conservative thresholds and can be disabled with runtime flag REDWOOD_ATTN_KERNEL_SELECTOR=off. Fused rotary kernel used only when model metadata reports rotary format. KV reservation is conservative and tunable. Rollout plan: gradual canary (10% traffic) for 48h then 50% -> 100% after monitoring.

Related: ENG-4412 (kernel selection), ENG-4475 (kv-cache hardening), small followups to SDKs will land separately to expose config flags.

Merge notes: squash merge after final perf sign-off.
